# ADR-012: Third-party notices are generated by an in-repo, dependency-free script over the lockfile

## Status
Accepted (2026-09-27, Task 46 close-out; the independent re-review approved
with non-blocking items. See `.agents/specs/review_report_task46.md`).
Proposed 2026-09-26 at the Task 46 Step 1 approval.

## Context
Guardrails #173-#176 require:
- a notice for every package the app ships;
- a fail-closed license allowlist;
- real license texts with cited overrides;
- reproducible output.

The shipped set is not "production dependencies". `mermaid` is a
**devDependency** (Task 45 B3) whose prebuilt `mermaid.min.js` is copied into
`dist/` and bundles its whole dependency tree. All 113 of those packages are
`"dev": true` in the lockfile. `github-markdown-css` and `highlight.js`
files are also copied into `dist/`. The closure is 125 packages.

## Decision
`scripts/third-party-notices.mjs` runs as the last step of `npm run build`
and writes `dist/third-party-notices.json`. It uses no dependencies and is
split into a pure core (unit-tested) and a thin IO shell.

- **Roots:**
  - the `package.json` `dependencies`;
  - a `BUILD_COPIED_PACKAGES` constant, which a unit test keeps equal to the
    `node_modules/<pkg>/` paths in the `build` script.
- **Closure:** follows `dependencies`, `optionalDependencies` and non-optional
  `peerDependencies`, resolved with Node's nested `node_modules` lookup over
  lockfile v3.
  - An unresolvable required edge fails the build.
  - An unresolvable optional edge is skipped.
- **Policy:** an ordered allowlist (`MIT`, `ISC`, `BSD-2-Clause`,
  `BSD-3-Clause`, `Apache-2.0`, `Python-2.0`, `Unlicense`).
  - `OR` passes on any allowed alternative. The first allowed alternative in
    allowlist order is recorded as `chosenLicense`.
  - `AND` requires every operand to be allowed.
  - Everything else fails: `WITH`, `+`, `LicenseRef-*`, `SEE LICENSE IN`,
    legacy field forms, and a missing license.
- **Texts:** every license and NOTICE file is reproduced verbatim from
  `node_modules`. Never generated from a template.
- **Overrides:** checked-in overrides (`build/third-party/`) with a pinned
  commit citation, machine-verified against the installed package on every
  build (`equals`/`contains`). Stale overrides fail the build.
- **Output:** deterministic (name, then numeric version, no timestamp).

## Alternatives considered
- **`license-checker` (rejected).** Unmaintained since 2019-01-10. Its
  `--production` filter drops all of Mermaid's tree, which is the omission
  #173 forbids. Without the filter it includes every devDependency, and we
  would need our own root filter anyway.
- **`license-checker-rseidelsohn`, `generate-license-file` (rejected).** Both
  are maintained, but they use the same production/development root model
  over the installed tree. Neither was found to verify override texts
  against the installed package or to require pinned citations. Both add a
  dependency tree to the build for logic we would still have to wrap.
- **Bundler license plugins (rejected).** We do not bundle Mermaid; we copy
  a prebuilt file, so no bundler ever sees its modules.
- **A pre-rendered HTML notices file (rejected).** It would move HTML
  escaping out of the single About renderer (#171). JSON plus escaping at
  render time keeps one escaping site.

## Consequences
- No new dependency is added (#179).
- A new or changed transitive package with a disallowed, missing or
  unparseable license fails `npm run build`, and therefore CI and release.
  The same happens when an override goes stale or its text drifts.
- A new copy-from-`node_modules` step in the build fails a unit test until
  the constant lists it.
- Deliberate over-inclusion: type-only packages such as
  `@types/trusted-types`, the `@types/d3-*` packages and `@chevrotain/types`
  are listed even though nothing bundles them.
